pick.name: Hinge Health, Inc.
pick.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on operating margin trend, six-month return against its sector, six-month return against spy — revenue +49.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield
evidence.period: trailing year against the reference close

pick.peerBasis: 113 candidates in SIC major group 73, compared on free cash flow yield, all from the same source and the same periods.

runnersUp.name: Travere Therapeutics, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was growth acceleration (-1.29)

runnersUp.name: Oscar Health, Inc.

runnersUp.name: Madison Square Garden Sports Corp.

pick.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 75.0× trailing earnings and a 3.5% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +47.2%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $62.16 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 100 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 100 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-08.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-04) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set
sources.prices: Massive (Polygon.io) grouped daily bars, splits and dividends

stories.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
stories.excerpt: Study finds coding efficiency gains get "absorbed" by human review "bottleneck."
stories.lead: The reason for that discrepancy can be found directly in the code review process, which takes markedly longer on average after the introduction of AI coding agents. Overall, the average “review process” time between a pull request getting submitted and it being merged into the codebase balloons 49 percent on average after AI agents are introduced. That effect can be seen in more granular data, too, with “the share of pull requests with changes requested nearly doubl[ing], and the number of comments per pull request increas[ing] by 35%” following the AI agent shift, the researchers write.

stories.title: Namespaces in Python
stories.excerpt: Python namespaces store and organize the symbolic names in your program. Learn when they're created, how they work, and how scope follows.
stories.lead:
A Python namespace is a mapping from names to objects. It works like a dictionary where keys are object names and values are the objects themselves. Namespaces organize variables and functions in a dedicated space, allowing you to use multiple instances of the same name without conflict, as long as they’re in different namespaces.

In this tutorial, you’ll explore the different types of namespaces in Python, including the built-in, global, local, and enclosing namespaces. You’ll also learn how they define the scope of names and influence name resolution in Python programs.

stories.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
stories.excerpt: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.
stories.lead:
For more on the science of healthy living, try NPR's Health newsletter.

Scientists have long marveled at how the human body tolerates extreme heat — and what that means for our health.

In the late 1700s, British scientists ran bold experiments on thermoregulation, subjecting themselves (and a dog) to a piping hot room and observing that — unlike the steak and eggs accompanying them — their own bodies did not cook.

stories.title: Delhi sees more protests as 'cockroach' group's leaders released
stories.excerpt: Police say they will keep restricting access to the city centre after thousands of people were detained and released on Saturday.
stories.lead:
A court in Indian capital Delhi has released the top leaders of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) as the city sees more protests for a second day with thousands of security personnel deployed and roads barricaded.

Abhijeet Dipke - who began the movement in May after India's Chief Justice likened some jobless young people to "cockroaches" - and other leaders were arrested on arrival in Delhi on Saturday to lead protests seeking electoral reforms.

In his first comments after his release, Dipke said "the CJP will neither back down nor be intimidated".

stories.title: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
stories.excerpt: The White House had blocked access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, leading them to restrict pool coverage.
stories.lead:
The US justice department (DoJ) has said it is investigating several TV networks over whether they broke federal competition laws when they recently suspended pool coverage of President Donald Trump.

Last month, five networks paused their presidential coverage for several days in response to the Trump administration withdrawing the credentials of reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico.

The justice department asked ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News to hand over communications related to the pool and said that the boycott could violate the Sherman Act, referring to a law that bars companies from engaging in monopolistic business practices.

Their statement says the dead on Saturday included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a…
stories.lead:
CAIRO (AP) — The latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday, with some in critical condition.

The attack was the deadliest in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi-backed government forces there.

stories.title: In one of the country's most competitive districts, a Democrat tries to keep her seat
stories.excerpt: In a highly competitive Washington congressional race, the incumbent Democrat has angered part of her party base and the Trump-backed Republican challenger faces backlash against the party in power.
stories.lead:
The fight for which party will control Congress is zoning in on one competitive district in southwest Washington state.

The 3rd Congressional District is a mix of urban, industrial and rural communities with inland and coastal areas. It prides itself on its political independence. President Trump won this congressional district three times. But Democratic Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez flipped the district blue in 2022. Now, the Republican nominee, state Sen. John Braun, believes he has a shot at winning it back.

stories.title: It's taking longer to find a new job after losing one
stories.excerpt: People who lose their jobs in this economy are taking longer to find new work. Nearly four in ten people exhaust their unemployment benefits before they land a new job.
stories.lead:
Evan Smith lost his job at a Colorado RV dealership this past spring after the company was sold. He's applied for numerous jobs since then, but hasn't found much traction.

"You find something that you're excited about or something that you think fits your profile and you go in and over 100 people have already clicked 'applied for it' in the last two weeks," Smith says. "So you just feel like you're a number."

stories.title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
stories.excerpt: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.
stories.lead:
When Harmeet Dhillon took over as the new chief of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division last April, the conservative attorney vowed to radically reshape the storied unit and its mission.

Over the past 18 months, Dhillon has moved aggressively to make that goal a reality. She has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many of them with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue President Trump's MAGA agenda, according to four current and former division officials.

Three of the individuals spoke on condition of anonymity out of fear of retribution.

Charities and businesses across the North East have said they are struggling with the rising cost of diesel.

The average price of diesel has risen above £2 a litre in the UK for the first time, according to the RAC motoring group.

Over the past seven months, the Iran war has severely disrupted the production and transportation of wholesale oil and refined products from the region, causing prices to surge worldwide.

stories.lead:
BRIDGEPORT, Pa. — The Colorado Mesa University men’s collegiate club team was recently awarded a 2026 Dr. Richard F. “Doc” Hunkler Grant.

The grant will be used to help build a sustainable collegiate water polo program in western Colorado by investing in long-term competition infrastructure and athlete development. The purpose of CMU’s project is to purchase permanent competition and training equipment that will strengthen athlete development while enhancing Colorado Mesa University’s ability to host high-quality collegiate water polo competitions via durable equipment that will benefit the program and the broader collegiate water polo community for years to come.
